column1: # job-selection-lint case table for auto-release.yml
# Format: <case-name> \t <context k=v;k=v> \t <expect-run csv> \t <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS, AND WHY IT EXISTS.
# auto-release.yml is the polymorphic DISPATCHER: `detect` classifies the repo,
# and exactly ONE per-language arm must select for that classification. Its
# entire selection surface is one context path — needs.detect.outputs.repo-type
# — so every row below declares that path and nothing else is needed to decide
# any job.
# The class of bug this table forecloses is the one this workflow has already
# shipped twice, both recorded in the workflow's own comments:
#   (1) before 2026-07-27 the `unsupported` catch-all gated on `== 'unknown'`
#       rather than a NEGATION of the dispatched set, so a repo detected as
#       ruby-gem / ansible-collection / github-action matched NO arm and no
#       catch-all: the run completed with zero jobs and reported GREEN while
#       publishing nothing. Rows `ruby-gem-repo`, `unknown-repo` and
#       `detect-emitted-nothing` are the ones that would have caught it — each
#       asserts `unsupported` RUNS, which is only true while the catch-all
#       stays a negation.
#   (2) an arm added to the file but left out of `unsupported`'s negation list
#       would double-select. Every row asserts every non-matching arm SKIPS, so
#       a new arm that forgets its negation clause turns this table red.
# Adding a dispatch arm therefore means adding its own row here AND appearing in
# the expect-skip column of all twelve other rows — that is deliberate friction
# on exactly the edit that broke this workflow before.
# PRIVACY IS NOT GATED IN THIS FILE — read this before looking for it.
# The sweep that produced this table exists because cargo-auto-release's `ship`
# job carries `&& !github.event.repository.private`, which silently no-published
# pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer on 2026-08-08. That guard is NOT here: this
# dispatcher's only `github.event.repository.private` reference is in `runs-on:`
# (runner routing), which is not a selection predicate and which this linter
# does not evaluate. The publish/no-publish decision happens ONE LEVEL DOWN,
# inside the reusable each arm calls, and is asserted in that workflow's own
# cases file (cargo-auto-release.cases.tsv et al) — not here.
# The `rust-single-crate-public` / `rust-single-crate-private` pair is kept
# anyway, and it is not decoration: it pins that DISPATCH is privacy-INDEPENDENT
# — the same arm is selected either way — so a future edit that tried to fix the
# silent-no-publish by short-circuiting the arm at this level (skipping
# rust-single-crate entirely on a private repo, which would trade a silent
# no-publish for a silent no-bump) fails this table instead of shipping.
# The privacy key is declared in those two rows and read by no condition; that
# is the point of the pair.
# `detect` has no `if:` and no `needs:`, so it selects in every case. It is
# named in every expect-run column rather than left unasserted, so a future
# `if:` added to it cannot pass unnoticed.
# CASES 1-10 — one row per type detect-repo-type emits that HAS a dispatch arm.
rust-workspace-repo
rust-single-crate-public
rust-single-crate-private
go-repo
npm-repo
python-repo
helm-repo
ansible-collection-repo
github-action-repo
caixa-repo
# CASES 11-13 — the three inputs that must reach the catch-all rather than fall
# through to a zero-job green run.
#   ruby-gem: emitted by detect-repo-type and DELIBERATELY armless (gem-release
#             declares RUBYGEMS_API_KEY required:true, which would re-create the
#             unsatisfiable secret union). It must fail loudly, not vanish.
#   unknown:  no recognized manifest at repo root.
#   empty:    detect ran but published no repo-type (a broken/changed
#             detect-repo-type). Distinct from 'unknown' — the action never said
#             so — and it must still land on the catch-all, not nowhere.
ruby-gem-repo
unknown-repo
detect-emitted-nothing
